title: United States Anti-Doping Agency Reauthorization Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

United States Anti-Doping Agency Reauthorization Act - Amends the Office of National Drug Control Policy Reauthorization Act of 2006 to: (1) authorize appropriations for the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency for FY2014-FY2020, (2) require that the Agency be recognized worldwide as the independent national anti-doping organization for the United States, and (3) replace the Agency's role in preventing the use by U.S. amateur athletes of performance-enhancing genetic modifications accomplished through gene doping with a role in preventing the use of prohibited performance-enhancing methods adopted by the Agency.

summary.headline: This 2014 law extends funding authorization for the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency through 2020, confirms its role as the nation's anti-doping organization, and shifts its focus on banned methods to those it adopts.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the 2006 Office of National Drug Control Policy Reauthorization Act to allow appropriations for the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency for fiscal years 2014 through 2020. It requires that the Agency be recognized worldwide as the independent national anti-doping organization for the United States. It also replaces the Agency's duty to prevent gene doping by amateur athletes with a duty to prevent prohibited performance-enhancing methods that the Agency itself adopts.

who_it_affects.how: They are covered by the Agency's anti-doping rules, and the methods they must avoid now include those the Agency adopts, instead of a focus on gene doping.
It can receive federal funding authorized for fiscal years 2014 through 2020 and is recognized as the official U.S. anti-doping organization worldwide.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 18, 2014; the summary does not list separate effective dates for each provision.
